summary: Deep investigation of auth stack completed. Converted the async test file to sync httpx (pytest-asyncio not installed in env) and expanded coverage to 19 tests covering the full review checklist: register email/username normalization + case collision + duplicate-key race, login case-insensitive + generic error + soft-lock (5 attempts, HTTP 423 with retry_after), forgot-password no-enumeration, reset-password one-time consumption + invalid/expired token, change-password old-password required (bypassed when must_change_password=True), /auth/me guard, legacy-bypass login for must_change users, IP throttle 429, referral-code ignored outside invite-only. 19/19 passed against preview URL. Backend fixes for email normalization + duplicate-key 400 + case-insensitive login all verified working. No backend bugs found.

minor.issue: IP-throttle key uses request.client.host which behind the k8s ingress is the backend pod IP, not the real client IP. Ingress round-robins between pods so a single attacker's attempts get split across per-pod counters, roughly doubling the effective threshold. Recommend deriving the key from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) to make the throttle truly per-client-IP.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Update login IP-throttle to key on X-Forwarded-For header so per-client throttling isn't diluted by multi-pod ingress round-robin.

(Optional/minor) The original test file used @pytest.mark.asyncio but pytest-asyncio is not installed — I rewrote it to sync httpx. Consider adding pytest-asyncio to requirements if async fixtures are wanted long-term.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py register() correctly normalizes email via .strip().lower() and catches duplicate-key exceptions to return 400 (verified via race-safe unique-index test flow).
auth.py login() correctly normalizes lookup email and returns generic 'Invalid email or password' for both unknown-email and bad-password branches.
Soft-lock triggers exactly at 5 failed attempts and returns 423 with retry_after=900 (15 min).
reset-password correctly clears must_change_password and marks token used_at so reuse returns 400.
change-password correctly enforces old_password unless must_change_password is set on the user.
Legacy bypass path audits into db.auth_audit, respects legacy_bypass_enabled toggle, and rejects blank passwords — all verified.
Minor: IP-throttle key `f"ip:{request.client.host}"` is not proxy-aware. Behind the k8s ingress the observed key is the backend pod IP, so attempts split across pods — recommend X-Forwarded-For.
test_credentials: admin@mercari.local / admin123 (unused in this run — all tests created fresh unique users)
seed_data_creation: Each test registers unique random users (email prefixes: Case_, UPPER_, login_, gen_, lock_, real_, cp_, me_, rst_, lb_, ref_). These stay in the users collection but are prefixed with random hex so they don't collide with real data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The 19-test auth suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_auth_deep_investigation.py (16 sync tests via public URL) and /app/backend/tests/test_auth_deep_investigation_db.py (3 tests that touch mongo directly for reset-token retrieval + must_change_password toggle + IP throttle). Both are pytest-xdist-safe (share the module-scoped httpx.Client via fixture). Run via `cd /app/backend && source .env && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... pytest tests/test_auth_deep_investigation*.py`. Note: pytest-asyncio is NOT installed in this env — write sync tests. Also note: the k8s ingress round-robins between two backend pods (10.79.139.10 / .11) which affects any test that relies on per-pod state like IP throttling; my test loops 40 times to reliably trigger 429 on at least one pod.
rca of the issue: All three fixes claimed by main agent verified working: (1) email lowercase normalization in register — verified via case-collision test + /auth/me returning lowercased email; (2) duplicate-key race protection — cannot deterministically race but the exception handler is present and covered by two duplicate-check tests; (3) case-insensitive login lookup — verified via register(upper) + login(lower/upper) both returning 200. No RCA needed — the fixes are correct. The only design-level observation is the IP-throttle key not being proxy-aware, which is a hardening improvement, not a bug.
